ROW.COLUMN: (FR/CU) Patterns of Funds Transfers: Customers and External Entities

Fraud schemes, particularly those involving multiple accounts or customers, can often be detected through the movement of funds between seemingly unrelated accounts. This could be indicative of a payments fraud or account takeover scheme, wherein the fraudster has gained access to a legitimate customer's account(s), or is initiating fraudulent debit transactions against the customer's accounts. The fraudster moves the funds out of the account and into accounts residing at other institutions, making recovery more difficult. This scenario identifies patterns of potentially suspicious activity between internal accounts and customers and external entities, such as high levels of activity or activity that indicates the existence of exclusive relationships between accounts and customers and external entities, and which could be indicative of fraudulent activity.

Scenario is realized as one pattern, but this pattern considers focal entity (Customer) - as two parties Originator party and Beneficiary Party, so the pattern will have two sets of datasets - for Originator and Beneficiary parties accordantly. The Originator set of datasets is the default set for scenario.
All alert-generating logic realized in Primary-Rule dataset. This dataset also provides Highlights and Scoring Bindings calculations. No Check-Points used in this pattern.
The Sub-Rules doesn't take part in behavior-detection logic and just provide supporting data for highlights and augmentation Instructions.
The first Sub-Rule is used to provide scenario Supporting Data (Display all electronic funds transaction records that are pertinent to the alert) and the second one to calculate '# of Accts' Highlight - Number of customer accounts involved in all matched transactions.
